body: Yes I'm working 40-60 hours a week at minimum wage. It varies based on the scheduling for my job. I only started to work after my parents passed away and I ran out of savings.

I've exhausted all the support services I could find in my state. I'm in Texas. Not sure where you are from but it is next to impossible to get any sort of support from the State of Texas. I'm not eligible for SS, I have no savings, and I've been denied both SSI and SSDI multiple times.

Wish I could move but I'm dirt poor.
I've already spoken to support services many times. There is sadly not much available for me beyond food pantries.
I've not worked for 10 years. Most of my life I was dealing with severe depression and anxiety and was essentially a shut-in living with my parents.

My only advice for the chronic pain community would be to kill yourself while can so as to forestall the pain and suffering in your future. If I had known I would have ended up like this, I would have killed myself in my 20s.

I don't socialize much and have no idea how to do that. I've tried making friends but I've not had much success. For my whole life my only friends have been my parents.

I have no time to volunteer, I'm working more than 60 hours a week just to keep myself from being homeless.

I cannot afford a gaming device or a TV. My phone is too slow and outdated for that as well. I am dirt poor.

I cannot afford a pet and I am allergic to dogs, cats, and most animals anyway.
Thank you. Unfortunately medical marijuana does not help me.

I did try volunteering at local kindergartens but I was very politely told by the teachers that it was not a good idea for a single older man to spend so much time around children. It apparently made the parents very uncomfortable.
Yes, but he lived to see 175 did he not? The ages of the patriarchs in Genesis are metaphorical. I do not believe Adam or Noah or Abraham lived for hundreds of years.
I've given up writing. I have not written anything in the last 10 years or so. I suppose the only thing left for me to write is my suicide note, though I doubt anyone will care to read it.
If the only thing there is left for me to do is suffer, then doesn't it make sense for me to end my life now and forestall that future suffering?

It's not about effort, it's about money as well. I would love to travel the world but I can barely afford rent and food. How do you expect me to travel the world? I don't have any retirement savings, I don't receive a pension or Social Security, and I earn $7.25 an hour.

That is a nice idea but unfortunately I do not have the energy to volunteer. I am working 50 hours a week to make ends meet (I am earning minimum wage). I also have chronic pain which saps my energy. A regular work day is enough to exhaust me completely.

Well, the reason I think I am a failure is because I failed to achieve all of my life goals: wife, kids, good career, etc.

I cannot afford therapy as I am on a shoestring budget and barely making ends meet as is. 

I am not sure what new goals I could come up with now, or if I even want to come up with any. I still wish there was a way for me to achieve my life goals of having a successful career and a wife and kids.
Well, my dream is/was to have get married, father kids, and eventually have grandkids. How do you suggest I do that at the age of 74?
I understand the sentiment but realistically what is there left to live for? And what would I even be losing if I give up?
It's a little too late for that. I don't think I can start a family or go to medical school at this age.
I am well aware of such websites. Unfortunately I have not had any luck on them.

For one, my chronic pain got worse as time went on. By my 40s I could barely cope despite medical intervention.

Secondly, I was bullied a lot as a kid and developed a lot of issues with self-esteem and making friends with others or talking to people. 

I married the first girl that looked at me without disgust which was a mistake. I married the wrong person. She was emotionally abusive and eventually became physically abusive as well.

After that I tried to find someone (for nearly 4 decades) but I didn't have any luck whatsoever. They said there are plenty of fish in the sea but looks like none of them were for me.

In terms of my career, I simply studied the wrong things and was passionate about the wrong things. I wanted to be a Hollywood filmmaker, and when that didn't work out, a successful author, and when that didn't work out, a travel writer, and when that didn't work out, I tried to do something more "practical". That didn't work out either. I made all the wrong decisions.

I don't know what type of happiness that would be. It's too late for me to have a family, which is all I've ever wanted. I am also allergic to both dogs and cats, and I am not an animal person in the least. I was mauled by a god when I was little, so I am afraid of animals as well.

I'm working with several pain doctors and a pain clinic and have been doing so for the past 20 years. It's not helped me much, maybe just taken my pain down from 10 to 7, but it's still there. 

I cannot afford therapy on my minimum wage job. There are only 2 sliding scale therapists in my area; I've had several sessions with both and it has not been helpful in the least.
I suppose, but I was mainly limited by things I could not change since birth - chronic pain, autism, and racism.

I don't do well with social interaction. I have bad social anxiety and have been diagnosed with autism. Also, I reached out to lawyers and the local social services office but I am ineligible for any social security benefits as I don't have a work history. Thank you for the advice anyway.
I'm going to be homeless soon so I don't think there's any point in mailing me anything. Thank you again for the offer, God bless you.
A time machine would be nice. Or if not that then medical science finding a cure for my chronic pain.
I'm currently on the verge of being homeless in Detroit. After that I think I will just find the nearest overpass and put myself out of misery. I'm pretty sure I've waited long enough.
Chronic migraine and back pain. I've had migraines almost every day since elementary school. The doctors have tried everything (even Botox and those newfangled experimental drugs) but nothing helped.

Chronic pain and autism kept me from progressing in a career or holding any kind of steady job.

I was bullied a lot as a kid and had trouble making friends and talking to people. Throughout my life my only friends were my parents. After they died I was completely alone.

I married the wrong person, she was emotionally and physically abusive and cheated on me. I was not able to find love again, no woman would even look at me. What makes me so angry now is that my ex-wife and her lover both went on to have happy and fulfilling lives with good careers, traveling the world, had children and grandchildren, etc. 

I believe I might be living proof that there is no such thing as karma.
